human_tolerance.notes: Judgement: breeds in open deciduous woods near openings, so not an urban species; Wikipedia says that in winter quarters it visits parks, gardens and feeders. Feeder use in the US is not sourced here.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Nest building from early May (Tennessee) to early June (Saskatchewan); egg laying to mid-July (Wikipedia, Breeding). Applies to the US range only.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Migrants leave in late September or October and return in late April or early May (Wikipedia, Migration). The 04-20 end is an approximate cut-off; the migrant status is from the Dryad row (migration = migrant).

vocalizations.description: Subdued, mellow warbling, a more refined and sweeter version of the American robin's song; males start singing early, sometimes in winter quarters.
Sharp 'pink' or 'pick' call. Wikipedia describes the call without an alarm function; using it as the alarm call is authored.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 2490494 (accepted, species). iNaturalist taxon 10271 (active, species rank). No Wikidata or ITIS key added; both are optional and were not checked.

range.note: Country-level from Wikipedia distribution text: breeds across Canada and the northeastern US, winters from central-southern Mexico through Central America and the Caribbean to Peru and Venezuela. Not exhaustive; the Caribbean and Colombia are described only loosely.

traits.limb_count.note: Birds have 2 walking limbs (legs), per the schema convention.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Fly from the flight description. Hop is for limb movement among branches and the rare ground use Wikipedia mentions; the species-local program uses hop only for feeding in foliage.

traits.flight.note: Migrates and flies between breeding and wintering ranges.

traits.nest_type.note: Nest is on a tree branch or over vines or elevated woody vegetation, an open cup. Nest type 'Cup'.

traits.perching.note: Forages in shrubs and trees and usually keeps to the treetops.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 42 g (Dunning08). Wikipedia gives 35-65 g with about 43 g in West Indies migrants and about 45 g in Pennsylvania banding; 42 g is the EltonTraits value.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of 29-33 cm span across the wings (Wikipedia, Description).

traits.lifespan_y.note: DERIVED PROXY, low confidence. Inputs: adult annual survival S = 0.553 (SE 0.049), Dryad row 274, mark-recapture, US (MAPS). Calculation: mean adult lifespan = 1/(1 - S) = 2.24 y, rounded to 2.2. Assumes constant annual adult survival, geometric lifetimes, and counting the year of death. Excludes first-year mortality, which pushes birth-to-death lifespan down, and treats apparent survival as true survival, which pushes it down too. Not the Wikipedia 'average maximum' 7.3 y or 'maximum recorded' 12 y 11 mo: those are maxima, not typical lifespans.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 50, Diet-Fruit 20, Diet-Seed 20, Diet-PlantO 10 (Ref_22, certainty A). PlantO is mapped to browse (buds and flowers, per Wikipedia). Wikipedia north-central US stomach contents: invertebrates 52%, wild fruit 19.3%, weed seed 15.7%, cultivated fruit 6.5%, other plant 6.5%, agree in broad terms.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia: fairly territorial in breeding; in winter small groups, sometimes flocks of a dozen or more.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal = 0 (not nocturnal); daytime song per Wikipedia.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: flees to cover, as with the perching songbird program.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement, not a measured value: 0.5, between the robin (0.2) and wary species. Wikipedia's 'shy' is the etymology of the genus, not behavioural evidence.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat: ground 20 (ground 0.2); understory+midhigh+canopy 80 (arboreal 0.8). Conflicts with Wikipedia 'only rarely can be seen on the ground'; the EltonTraits value is used because it is quantitative and CC0. Treat the ground share as uncertain.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Judgement: roosts in dense woody cover. No roost-site source was checked.

habitat.resources.note: Weights from the diet split. Nest_cup (open cup in trees or shrubs, 0.8-16.7 m, average 6 m) from Wikipedia Breeding. Shelter tags are judgement. Months: insects in breeding months, fruit in late summer, nest_cup in May-July.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement from Wikipedia: breeds in open deciduous woods, visits parks and gardens in winter quarters. Urban affinity is not measured.

seasonal.strategy.note: Dryad row classes the species as a migrant; Wikipedia describes a migration to tropical America in winter.

seasonal.phases.note: Dates from Wikipedia Breeding and Migration; US-specific cut-offs are approximate.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration 21 days from 'independent of their parents after approximately 3 weeks'. Scale 0.8 is judgement.

vocalizations.song.note: Wikipedia Description: subdued mellow warbling; males start singing early. Season and time windows are authored.

vocalizations.alarm.note: Wikipedia describes the sharp pink or pick call but not its alarm function. Authored as the alarm call; not verified.

look.note: Judgement, from the Wikipedia plumage description: male black head, back and wings; rose-red breast; white underparts. A single palette cannot show both sexes.

behavior.note: Species-local program bt-pheucticus-ludovicianus-v1 (behavior.json). A copy of bt-perching-songbird-v1 with nesting moved to May-July (shared program hard-codes April and May), insect food only in May-August, fruit otherwise, and hop feeding kept as a limitation.
